prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Restaurant Dinner Menu (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Starters" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Mains" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Desserts" spans 4 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Dish" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 164px
  col 2: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 558px
  col 3: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 37px
  col 4: header "Allergens" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 298px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Help diners choose dishes by comparing their descriptions, prices and allergens within each course.","reading":"Readers scan course headings and dish names first, then read across a row for details; the course headings span the full table and should remain distinct from dish rows.","groups":["Dish and Description belong together as the name and explanation of each menu item.","Price and Allergens are compact decision aids that readers compare across dishes."],"keep_intact":["Price values and the Price header","Individual words in dish names, descriptions and allergen lists","The association between each dish and its price and allergens"],"may_wrap":["Descriptions can wrap naturally at word spaces.","Multiword dish names can wrap when needed.","Allergen lists can wrap at natural breaks; description wrapping may already provide enough row height to accommodate them."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[185,340,58,136],"idea":"Keep dish names on one line, give descriptions most of the remaining space, and allow allergen lists to wrap."},{"name":"B","widths":[150,310,58,201],"idea":"Give allergens more room for easier comparison, accepting some wrapping in dish names and descriptions."},{"name":"C","widths":[120,400,58,141],"idea":"Prioritize flowing descriptions by using a narrow dish-name column and letting longer names wrap."}]}
